newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-DYNAMO KIEV WIN FIFTH SUCCESSIVE TITLE IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DYNAMO KIEV WIN FIFTH SUCCESSIVE TITLE IN STYLE.

text.p: Dynamo Kiev, the most successful side in Soviet soccer, clinched their fifth successive Ukrainian league title on Friday with a crushing 6-1 victory over Zirka-Nibas Kirovohrad.
The home win gave Dynamo an unbeatable 15-point lead over second-placed Shakhtar Donetsk with four games left to play.

The comfortable reassertion of Dynamo's supremacy at home gives newly returned chief coach Valery Lobanovsky the springboard he needs to try and recapture the club's glory days in European competition.

Lobanovsky, who led Kiev to the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1975 and left shortly before they lifted the same trophy in 1986, returned early this year with a pledge to build a new team capable of European success.

The resources at his disposal are much reduced from the heady days of old, when Kiev dominated the Soviet league. But Ukrainian fans hope the 57-year-old former Soviet national coach can erase memories of Dynamo's disgrace in 1995, when they were thrown out of the Champions' League over a match-fixing scandal.
A three-year banned was commuted but the club went out in the first round of this season's UEFA to modest Neuchatel.
